propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, and rotation concerns with no cohesive ownership, making safety rules fragmented and production code mutate bindings through a shallow compatibility query.

The extraction must preserve byte-for-byte compatibility (indent=2, sorted keys, trailing newline, unknown fields) and all five-file selective publication behavior while decomposing into repository, lifecycle, and recovery owners behind one unchanged public facade.

Durable tombstones represent authoritative retirement intent and should only be revoked by explicit unretire; automatic liveness observations must never resurrect a tombstoned identity, and completion requires all three (tombstone, forward, reverse) identities to agree.

Live recovery must run after configuration and staleness validation but before remote issue observation, then remain idempotent so preview/dry-run modes never perform remote mutations or local state writes.

The extraction is unsafe unless held-out RED-first tests for 15+ fault/corruption cases pass unseen, and mutation testing catches oracle gaps (shallow-copy aliasing, comment identity loss, spy instrumentation blindness) that characterization tests cannot detect.
